R6D-bear-backcountry-0001.name: By Standard Creek
R6D-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R6D-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2017 (9 years old), 130 m SE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SW facing slope, 12 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Standard Creek 90 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

flags.t: Route crosses private land (ParcelMap BC, updated 2026-10-02): get permission first or go around.

plan: Drive: from District of Port Edward, about 34 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 53.94416, -130.07078, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 10 km N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 388 m, about 242 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 200 m E of the spot at 215 m (54.0353, -130.05855). Water: Standard Creek 20 m NW (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-11, Region 6. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-02, closures 2026-10-16.
R6D-bear-backcountry-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-11: about 221 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.01 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
